thread.title_full: League MVP from Hingham has the 'clutch gene' for BC High baseball - NewsBreak

author: Jason Snow
title: League MVP from Hingham has the 'clutch gene' for BC High baseball - NewsBreak
text:
By Jason Snow The Patriot Ledger ,
1 days ago DORCHESTER — Scoop. Plant. Throw.
When Brody Beale did so on a hot-shot ground ball as an eighth-grade shortstop five years ago, it caught the eye of BC High baseball coach Steve Healy .
“I was like, ‘Wow. Kid’s got a cannon,'" Healy said.
Beale, a Hingham resident, went on to play on the BC High junior varsity team during his freshman campaign and then he earned the starting job on Healy's state-championship team as a sophomore in 2024. He's held down the position ever since.
Last year, Beale was not one of the four BC High players to receive Catholic Conference All-Star honors. He elevated as a senior this spring to capture the league's MVP award before he treks on to a Division 1 college career at the University of Rhode Island.
"Brody is by far one of the best fielders I've seen," said senior pitcher Adam Bushley, who hails from Cohasset. "Off the field, he's a leader through and through."
When Beale first cracked the varsity roster as a sophomore, he carved out a role in the bottom half of Healy's lineup. He batted ninth in the Division 1 state final, a 5-1 win over St. John's (Shrewsbury), at Polar Park in Worcester. This year, Healy slots him in "anywhere in the top 4," the coach said, and Beale came through with 20 RBIs on the season.
On May 22, Beale drove in the winning run on a walk-off base hit to defeat St. John's, a victory that decided the Catholic Conference title race. Healy said his shortstop "has the clutch gene, but his defense is what makes him special.”
"He's gotten a lot bigger," said senior left fielder Andrew Flaherty, of Lakeville. "The power he has in his back now is a big difference from last year. ... He's gotten into the role of being a leader really well and he put the team first."
"(My journey) has been awesome, but the record is more important," Beale said. "Winning the Catholic Conference championship is what we wanted at the start of the year and of course we strive to win a state championship eventually. That's just what we're all going for."
The Eagles claimed their fourth state title (2001, '08, '09, '24) during Beale's sophomore season, and last year, were ousted in the Sweet Sixteen at the end of another showdown against St. John's (15-8 final).
This year's squad (19-2), which earned the No. 1 seed in the state tournament, is headlined by a core of 16 seniors. The Eagles' opened their postseason push with an 8-2 victory over No. 33 Methuen (8-2 final) at home on Sunday, May 31, in which Beale charged four ground balls on the move and fired over to first base for the out.
Said Healy, “When he makes one of those plays on the run, throwing off of one foot and it’s chest-high to (Sam) Bushley (at first base), I’m like, ‘I’m going to miss that next year.’ ...
“Hopefully we get him for another four more games and we can finish this.”
THEY SAID IT Healy on Beale: “There’s not a situation that he hasn’t been involved with or seen. That senior leadership and experience separates him from so many other guys.”
Beale on motivation after last year's Sweet Sixteen exit: "We got something taken from us that we wanted last year. We wanted to carry on and make something special. ... That lit a flame under all of us to get going for this year."
Flaherty: "When we were handing our jerseys in (last year), we all agreed to buy into the process. You see the first game til now, we've had a lot of success, but it started way before that. The time we put in the weight room and the meetings after school really helped us be the team we are now. We're showing it."
